title: Contract-based router linter & staged validation refactor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Our current routing DSL validator mixes syntactic checks with environment-aware safety heuristics which makes rule authors receive noisy errors and blocks staged rollouts. This ticket refactors the policy engine's validation pipeline into explicit contract stages (syntax -> type/shape -> contract bindings -> capacity & fallback safety) and introduces a lightweight linter that surfaces actionable autofix suggestions for common misconfigurations. Scope: internal validator refactor, lint rules, compatibility matrix checks for model variants, region-affinity and tier-scoring sanity checks, and migration tooling for existing routing configs. Non-goals: changing rule semantics or routing runtime behavior beyond safety catches; UI console changes (handled in separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Validation pipeline broken into four distinct stages with clear error categories: syntax, schema/type, contract-binding, and runtime-safety checks
New linter produces machine-readable findings and autofix suggestions for >= 40 common misconfigs (e.g., missing variant tag, ambiguous region selector, unsupported quantization variant)
Fallback compatibility matrix validator rejects configs where a primary model variant cannot be safely substituted by any listed fallback under defined constraints
Unit and integration tests exercising region selection edge cases (multi-region tie-breakers, regional capacity signals mocked) with >= 95% coverage for new validator modules
Migration tool (config-migrate-v2) can upgrade 95% of existing routing rules without manual edits; remaining items produce clear, actionable migration hints
New metrics emitted to telemetry: policy.validation.errors.by_stage, policy.lint.autofix_attempts, policy.deployment.blocked_reasons; dashboards updated reference links in attachments
No runtime latency change in policy evaluation path for accepted configs (measure baseline) beyond +1ms median allowed for safety checks
Code review approved by runtime, infra, and security code owners; release flagged behind feature gate for staged rollout
design_notes: Introduce ValidatorFacade that dispatches rule definitions through ordered stages. Each stage returns typed findings with severity and suggested fix metadata.

Contract-binding stage will evaluate rule variable substitutions (model catalog IDs, region aliases, tier labels) against a snapshot of the model catalog and region capacity hints; snapshot versioning avoids flapping errors during deploys.

Runtime-safety stage includes: fallback-compatibility check (ensures fallback variant accepts same input/output shapes and is available in target regions), tier-affinity sanity (ensures reserved capacity tiers are not targeted by low-tier-only rules), and cold-start risk scoring.

Linter CLI will be published as redwood-policy-lint v1 with a --autofix flag. Autofix will only adjust non-semantic fields (normalizing region aliases, expanding shorthand variant lists) and will create a migration suggestions file for manual review for anything potentially risky.
Introduce a small sampling harness that runs a policy simulation DAG using production-like distributions (stored as fixtures) to catch nondeterministic ordering issues in region tie-breakers.
Validation errors are categorized and include stable error codes (e.g., RP-1001: MISSING_FALLBACK_VARIANT, RP-2003: REGION_AMBIGUOUS_SELECTOR) to allow automated policy gate tooling to react.
Security review: ensure validator never resolves to secrets or KMS calls. Contract-binding snapshots are read-only and audited.
Observability: emit counts per error code and time-to-fix tag when autofix used. Add dashboard widgets for top failing config patterns and migration backlog size.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Run redwood-policy-lint --check across all production config repos to gather baseline findings (run as nightly job).
Phase 1: Apply --autofix for safe, idempotent edits to a small pilot org (internal services) and validate behavior via integration tests and canary traffic.
Phase 2: Run config-migrate-v2 in dry-run across customer-managed config stores; collect remaining manual edits and generate migration playbook.
Phase 3: Enable feature gate for staged rollout; block policy deploys with high-severity findings for opt-in orgs; allow warning-only mode for others for 4 weeks before enforcement.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary: 2 internal teams (platform, console) run migrated configs behind feature gate
Week 1: telemetry sanity checks and rollback window (48 hours).
Week 2-3: expand to 10% of customer orgs as opt-in via Console toggle.
Week 4: enforce high-severity blocks for new policy pushes; continue warning-only for legacy orgs for 30 days, then full enforcement
Provide runbook: policy-rollout-rollback.md (attachments) and add an on-call rotation with runtime team during rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overzealous validator blocks valid, complex policies -> Mitigation: warning-only mode and opt-in enforcement for first 4 weeks; staged schema versions.
Risk: Autofix changes introduce semantic drift -> Mitigation: restrict autofix to normalization only and require manual sign-off for anything that programmatically expands or removes variant lists.
Risk: Catalog snapshot staleness causes false positives -> Mitigation: snapshot version included in validation findings; validator can operate in 'pin snapshot' or 'live-lookup' mode for debugging.
Risk: Increased CI time for linting -> Mitigation: provide a fast-check mode that only runs syntax+schema locally and run heavyweight contract checks as part of server-side CI.
Risk: Telemetry cardinality from many unique rule errors -> Mitigation: bucketize error contexts and emit sampling for high-cardinality fields.
